articles.headline: Inside the NFL's wild endings and why coaches need to adapt
articles.description: Scoring too early and kicking the ball into the end zone can be costly, as the Cowboys learned.

images.name: Spencer Shrader [1296x729]
images.caption: Spencer Shrader's field goal put the Colts up 19-17 over the Texans with 16 seconds left, and Shrader made sure to not give Houston a touchback. The Texans took over at their 31 with 11 seconds left and couldn't convert.

images.name: Zay Flowers [1296x729]
images.caption: Zay Flowers' 27-yard gain left one second on the clock, which was enough for the Ravens to kick a game-winning field goal against the Cowboys.

images.name: Cam Little [1296x729]
images.caption: Guys like Jacksonville's Cam Little, who's kicked two field goals over 60 yards -- including a record 68-yarder -- put the burden on teams not to leave much time on the clock and not to kick the ball into the end zone.

images.name: Tyler Loop [1296x729]
images.caption: Tyler Loop's 56-yarder as time expired showed what happens when you leave too much time on the clock and kick the ball into the endzone.
